acme-maps-engineer: Hey team — our ingestion pipeline to Pinecone started throwing dimension mismatch errors about 30m ago after we enabled batching. Not every batch fails, maybe ~1/5. Error looks like: 
```
Error: vector dimension mismatch. expected 1536 but got 1024 (item index 37)
```
We call Redwood embeddings endpoint via our worker pool with batch_size=8. Request id from our logs: rwd-req-0a7f9 (attached below). Any suggestions? We can revert to batch_size=1 but that kills throughput.

sarah (Support): Thanks — can you paste the original request payload (no PII) and the exact model param you're sending? Also please include the Redwood request id/trace if you have it (rwd-... as you pasted). In the meantime, try one direct call (no pooling) and reply with the embedding vector length. :mag_right:

acme-maps-engineer: Here's a minimal repro we ran locally (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-large","input":["road segment A","road segment B","road segment C"]}'
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0012, -0.023, ...], "index":0}, {"embedding":[0.0010, ...], "index":1}, {"embedding":[0.0009, ...], "index":2}], "model":"redwood-emb-large-2026-03-09"}
```
When we run `len(response.data[0].embedding)` in Python we sometimes get 1536 and sometimes 1024 across different runs. That's what makes me think routing or a variant flip. Trace header we forwarded from the worker is: trace_id=trace-1964023000-rwd-0a7f9.

mike (Eng-ML): Thanks, this is helpful. Quick checks: 1) Are you pinning the `model` to a specific version (e.g., `redwood-emb-large@v1`)? If not, automated variant rollouts can route you to a different size/dim model. 2) Can you paste the full `model` string the client sends? If it's just `redwood-emb-large` the platform may choose a compatible variant at runtime.

acme-maps-engineer: We just pass `redwood-emb-large` (no explicit @version). We saw a change around 2026-03-10 17:20 UTC which correlates with the first failures. We also attached a short trace snippet from the Redwood console (we redacted tokens): 
```
TRACE: trace-1964023000-rwd-0a7f9
route: embeddings -> redwood-emb-large-v2 (1024d)
  auth: 5ms
  routing: 18ms
  model_exec: 38ms
  serialization: 4ms
  network: 11ms
```

sarah (Support): That trace confirms routing to a v2 variant which is 1024d. Two quick options: - pin the model to a specific version to keep 1536d (if you need it) OR - change your downstream vector DB schema to accept 1024d for this dataset. We can help pin or roll you back.

mike (Eng-ML): Adding detail: we rolled a compact variant (v2) yesterday that outputs 1024 dims for lower latency/cost. We default-route for throughput-optimized customers. There should be no probabilistic mix for a single customer unless you are on a policy that allows `compatible` fallbacks or multi-variant routing. The intermittent behavior suggests your requests sometimes hit a node still pinned to the older variant or some caching in the routing layer.

acme-maps-engineer: OK that explains it. Two follow-ups: 1) why does it only happen when batch_size > 1? We have a hunch a single-item request always hits the same fast path. 2) can you provide a per-request latency breakdown in the dashboard so we can correlate failed batches with routing decisions?

tom (Eng-SRE): On the batching:_BATCHING + routing interplay: our runtime can route batched requests to the least-loaded variant that can satisfy the request. If the variants differ in embedding_dim, the runtime normally expands/trims are not allowed — we should not mix dims in a batch. Intermittent failures could be due to a race where the router accepted a batch but backend selector changed between items. That's a bug if true.

sre-bot: Deploy event detected: embeddings-router v1.43 rolled at 2026-03-10T17:18:42Z across region-us-east-1. Rollout-strategy: gradual (10% -> 100%). Affected routes: embeddings (policy=compatible).

mike (Eng-ML): Action plan: 1) We'll check the router logs around that rollout for partial weights. 2) For immediate mitigation, set batch_size=1 or explicitly set `model: "redwood-emb-large@v1"` in your client to pin dimension. 3) We'll add a check in the router to reject mixed-dim batches (if missing) — assigning to eng-runtime.

acme-maps-engineer: Can you also show the per-request latency breakdown you mentioned? Even a small example for a single failing batch would help us. We need to know whether auth/routing/model_exec is spiking.

mike (Eng-ML): Example trace from the failing batch (console link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-1964023000-rwd-0a7f9 ):
```
auth: 6.2ms
routing.lookup: 21.1ms
routing.variant_select: 9.7ms
queue.wait: 12.3ms
model.tokenize: 3.8ms
model.exec: 47.4ms
serialize: 5.2ms
network: 10.9ms
```
model variant selected: redwood-emb-large-v2 (1024d)

mike (Eng-ML): The critical observation: routing.variant_select and queue.wait timing aligns with rollout windows. When the rollout is mid-progress, different items in a batch can be routed to different nodes. We'll follow up with eng-runtime to make batch selection atomic.

acme-maps-engineer: Appreciate the quick triage. We'll flip batch_size to 1 for ingestion right now. Please keep us posted on rollback or router fix. Also can you add a dashboard panel to show the output dimension for recent embedding calls per model id? That would have helped us detect this earlier.

dashboard-bot: New dashboard saved: "embeddings: output_dim histogram by model" (url: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/emb-dim-hist-1964023000) — visibility: support + eng-runtime + customer-acme-maps.

tom (Eng-SRE): Internal TODOs: - eng-runtime to add rejection for mixed-dim batches (high) - eng-ml to review rollout policy (med) - support to advise customers about pinning and best-practice batching (low) - add automated alert if output_dim changes for a model (low)

mike (Eng-ML): I'll own the router fix. ETA: 48h for hotfix to ensure atomic variant selection for batches; will post progress here. For now, pin the model or set batch_size=1.

acme-maps-engineer: Thanks all — pinning now and will report back after verifying ingestion. Will keep the thread open until fix is in. :thumbsup:
